note:
Mismatches with HANDOFF.md, as observed on this host (macOS x86_64, Python 3.12.16, no Lean):

1. 19b and 19g are listed as "any host with Python 3.12", with no install step. Run exactly as written with a clean Python 3.12, both crash at import before verifying anything: evidence19b.py / evidence19g.py -> lane.py / drill19.py -> gate19.py -> assurance-composed-successor/successor.py -> assurance-composed/composition.py -> assurance-signals/signals.py line 13 `import openai` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai'. Exit 1, nothing on stdout. HANDOFF.md only mentions a venv for 19a --replay.

2. The handoff's venv recipe (pip install --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -r tools/assurance-sdk/requirements.lock -r tools/assurance-workflow/requirements.lock) cannot install on macOS x86_64: "No matching distribution found for cryptography==50.0.2" (no wheel for this platform). As written it is Linux x86_64-only, which HANDOFF.md says for --replay but which also makes it unusable as a workaround for item 1 on a Mac.

3. Workaround used for the second run of 19b and 19g: a fresh venv from the same Python 3.12.16 with only openai==3.31.0 and its dependencies (annotated-types, anyio, certifi, distro, h11, httpcore, httpcore2, httpx, httpx2, idna, jiter, pydantic, pydantic-core, sniffio, truststore, typing-extensions, typing-inspection), each taken with its hashes from tools/assurance-sdk/requirements.lock and installed with --require-hashes --only-binary=:all:. Nothing in the repository was edited. The verifier_output given for 19b and 19g is from that second run.

4. 19d refused with RuntimeError: host_cannot_namespace (traceback, exit 1, no JSON), as HANDOFF.md predicts for a non-Linux host.

5. 19a was run without --replay (not Linux x86_64; locked venv not installable). Its receipt reports replay: not_requested / not_run.

6. Lean was absent, so 19b's Lean fields are expected as null / false (see 19b's not_compared).

7. The test suite (about 30 minutes) was not run.

Custody: the operator (Michael) ran this alone on a Mac the author has never touched. The author did not access the machine, see the session or take part in the run, and supplied nothing beyond the handoff zip listed above. The repository was cloned fresh from https://github.com/Raoof128/Project-Simurgh.git at the commit, with full history. For completeness: the operator used Claude Code (an AI coding agent) to type and run the commands, on a Claude subscription registered to the author.
